top.name: Let S(x,y) = number of lattice paths from (0,0) to (x,y) that use the step set { (0,1), (1,0), (2,0), (3,0), ...} and never pass below y = x. Sequence gives S(n-1,n) = number of 'Schröder' trees with n+1 leaves and root of degree 2.

web.query: maximum number of bonds among n atoms in the diamond lattice, cluster with fewest dangling bonds, edge-isoperimetric problem diamond lattice
web.found: edge-isoperimetric results for Z^d (Bollobas and Leader), the triangular, square, hexagonal and cubic lattices (N^(3/4) laws for the minimisers), Barber and Erde for Cayley graphs on Z^d, and Strachan and Swanepoel, Edge isoperimetry of lattices (arXiv:2503.09591: Cayley graphs on Z^d and the triangular lattice); nothing on the diamond lattice

web.query: diamondoid C_nH_m fewest hydrogen atoms for a given number of carbon atoms, diamond lattice, most compact hydrocarbon fragment, nanodiamond minimum hydrogens
web.found: the catamantane formula C(4n+6)H(4n+12) (Balaban and Rucker), an enumeration of the diamondoids CnHm with 10 to 41 carbon atoms (nomenclature, stabilities, gaps; 2018), CH and CH2 counts of truncated tetrahedral nanodiamonds (arXiv:2111.04490); no fewest-hydrogen values over all fragments of the diamond lattice

web.query: hydrogenated silicon nanocrystal Si_nH_m minimum number of hydrogen atoms for given n, optimal shape, diamond lattice cluster, dangling bonds, minimal surface
web.found: structures of SinH2m clusters with n <= 21 (Nanoscale 2021) and work on amorphous and nanocrystalline silicon; no extremal dangling-bond counts
